tables.name: branches
tables.description: One row per library branch in the network.

columns.name: branch_id
columns.doc: Branch number used across the system.

columns.name: branch_name
columns.doc: Name the branch goes by.

columns.name: city
columns.doc: Town or city where the branch is located.

columns.name: opened
columns.doc: Year the branch first opened to the public.

columns.name: floor_area
columns.doc: Public floor space of the branch, in square feet.

columns.name: visitors
columns.doc: Average number of visitors counted at the door per month during 2026.

tables.name: books
tables.description: One row per book title in the catalogue.

columns.name: book_id
columns.doc: Catalogue number of the title.

columns.name: title
columns.doc: Title of the book.

columns.name: author
columns.doc: Author's full name.

columns.name: category
columns.doc: Shelving category: 1 = non-fiction, 2 = reference, 3 = adult fiction, 4 = children's.

columns.name: pub_year
columns.doc: Year this edition was published.

tables.name: copies
tables.description: One row per physical copy of a book held by a branch.

columns.name: copy_id
columns.doc: Barcode number of the physical copy.

columns.name: book_id
columns.doc: Title this copy is a copy of.

columns.name: branch_id
columns.doc: Branch the copy belongs to.

columns.name: condition
columns.doc: Physical state of the copy: 1 = worn, 2 = withdrawn from stock, 3 = good, 4 = new.

columns.name: acquired_on
columns.doc: Date the library bought the copy, written YYYY-MM-DD.

tables.name: members
tables.description: One row per registered library member.

columns.name: member_id
columns.doc: Library card number.

columns.name: full_name
columns.doc: Member's full name.

columns.name: kind
columns.doc: Membership type: 1 = adult, 2 = junior (under 16), 3 = staff, 4 = senior (65 and over).

columns.name: joined
columns.doc: Date the member first registered, written YYYY-MM-DD.

columns.name: branch_id
columns.doc: Member's home branch.

tables.name: loans
tables.description: One row per time a copy was lent to a member.

columns.name: loan_id
columns.doc: Reference number of the loan.

columns.name: copy_id
columns.doc: Copy that was lent out.

columns.name: member_id
columns.doc: Member who borrowed the copy.

columns.name: loaned_on
columns.doc: Date the copy was lent out, written YYYY-MM-DD.

columns.name: due_on
columns.doc: Date the copy has to be back, written YYYY-MM-DD.

columns.name: returned_on
columns.doc: Date the copy was brought back, written YYYY-MM-DD, or 9999-12-31 while it is still out.

tables.name: fines
tables.description: One row per fine charged against a loan.

columns.name: fine_id
columns.doc: Reference number of the fine.

columns.name: loan_id
columns.doc: Loan the fine was charged for.

columns.name: reason
columns.doc: Why the fine was charged: 1 = damaged copy, 2 = overdue return.

columns.name: amount
columns.doc: Fine charged, in pence.

columns.name: state
columns.doc: Payment state: 1 = waived, 2 = unpaid, 3 = paid.

questions.sql: SELECT branch_name FROM branches WHERE city = 'Leeds'

questions.text: Which author has the most titles in our catalogue?
questions.sql: SELECT author FROM books GROUP BY author ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

questions.text: Name the branches that get over 100,000 visitors a year.
questions.sql: SELECT branch_name FROM branches WHERE visitors * 12 > 100000

needs_docs.fact: the figure is an average per month, so multiply by 12 to get a yearly total

questions.text: Show me every branch with more than 700 square metres of public space.
questions.sql: SELECT branch_name FROM branches WHERE floor_area * 0.092903 > 700

needs_docs.fact: floor space is in square feet, so multiply by 0.0929 to get square metres

questions.text: How many children's titles do we hold?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM books WHERE category = 4

questions.text: Count the copies that have been withdrawn from stock.
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM copies WHERE condition = 2

needs_docs.fact: condition 2 means the copy was withdrawn from stock

questions.text: How many of our members are under 16?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM members WHERE kind = 2

needs_docs.fact: type 2 is the junior membership, for members under 16

questions.text: How many fines are still waiting to be paid?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fines WHERE state = 2

needs_docs.fact: state 2 means the fine is unpaid

questions.text: What was the biggest single fine, in pounds?

needs_docs.fact: amounts are in pence, so divide by 100 to get pounds

questions.text: How many copies are out on loan right now?
questions.sql: SELECT COUNT(*) FROM loans WHERE returned_on = '9999-12-31'

needs_docs.fact: the date 9999-12-31 is a placeholder meaning the copy has not been returned yet

ambiguous.text: Which branch is the most heavily used?

readings.gloss: its copies were lent out the most times
readings.sql: SELECT b.branch_name FROM loans l JOIN copies c ON c.copy_id = l.copy_id JOIN branches b ON b.branch_id = c.branch_id GROUP BY b.branch_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT branch_name FROM branches ORDER BY visitors DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: Branch usage is judged by how many times its copies are lent out.

ambiguous.text: What is our most popular book?

readings.sql: SELECT bk.title FROM loans l JOIN copies c ON c.copy_id = l.copy_id JOIN books bk ON bk.book_id = c.book_id GROUP BY bk.book_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

readings.gloss: borrowed by the most different members
readings.sql: SELECT bk.title FROM loans l JOIN copies c ON c.copy_id = l.copy_id JOIN books bk ON bk.book_id = c.book_id GROUP BY bk.book_id ORDER BY COUNT(DISTINCT l.member_id) DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: A book's popularity is its total number of loans, regardless of who borrowed it.

ambiguous.text: How much money do we make from fines?

readings.gloss: only fines that were paid, in pounds
readings.sql: SELECT SUM(amount) / 100.0 FROM fines WHERE state = 3

resolving_note.text: Income from fines means the fines that members have actually paid.

readings.sql: SELECT branch_name FROM branches ORDER BY floor_area DESC LIMIT 1
SELECT b.branch_name FROM copies c JOIN branches b ON b.branch_id = c.branch_id GROUP BY b.branch_id ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: A branch's size is its public floor space.

ambiguous.text: Which book in our collection is the oldest?

readings.sql: SELECT title FROM books ORDER BY pub_year ASC LIMIT 1

readings.gloss: copy held by the library the longest
readings.sql: SELECT bk.title FROM copies c JOIN books bk ON bk.book_id = c.book_id ORDER BY c.acquired_on ASC LIMIT 1

resolving_note.text: A book's age is counted from its publication year.
